Internazionale (Italy) carrying Reuters wire copy — 30 September 2026. *** INTERNAZIONALE IS NOT AN APPROVED DOMAIN — DO NOT CITE. ***
This file exists ONLY to record material that is in the Reuters wire but which I could not retrieve from an approved carrier, so Ed can hunt for the Reuters original (reuters.com IS approved; WebFetch 403s on it and Exa's crawler returned CRAWL_NOT_FOUND for my constructed URL guesses, so I never verified the reuters.com URL and have deliberately not written one down).

Reuters dateline: "BRUSSELS, Sept 30 (Reuters)". Reporters named in other carriers of the same wire: Lili Bayer and Andrew Gray in Brussels, Mark Trevelyan in London, Reuters in Moscow; editing by Timothy Heritage.

MATERIAL NOT AVAILABLE FROM ANY APPROVED OUTLET I COULD REACH:

1) NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, speaking at a defence conference in Brussels hosted by broadcaster Euronews, on NATO's reply to Moscow:
   "We are a defensive alliance. And stop the nuclear threats. This is absolutely not called for and not helpful."

2) Rutte, asked if the risk of nuclear weapons being used against the Baltics was now real:
   "No, it's not. Putin knows that he can never win (against) NATO, so I don't take this that seriously."

3) The non-paper's own words, as quoted by Reuters:
   - NATO is pursuing a "dangerous and reckless course" entailing "high risks of the outbreak of a direct armed conflict".
   - That includes the possibility "of Russian strikes against decision-making centers in the alliance's member states right from the outset of the conflict".
   - "Russia will be ready to use the entire arsenal of forces and capabilities at its disposal, including nuclear weapons, in order to defend its territory should NATO countries undertake any attempt aimed at isolating the Kaliningrad Region from the rest of the country."

4) NATO's written response, seen by Reuters: none of its "exercises or activities pose a threat to the territory of the Russian Federation"; "We call upon the Russian Federation to end its unprovoked full-scale invasion of Ukraine. We urge the Russian Federation to refrain from increasingly reckless behaviour towards the Allies and to cease its irresponsible nuclear rhetoric."

5) A senior European defence official (unnamed): "(This is the) first time since (the) Cold War that Russia is threatening us like this. So this is serious."

6) A NATO diplomat (unnamed): "I would say that the Russian letter is only another Russian attempt to intimidate Europeans, and that the response by NATO is firm and responsible. (It) reaffirms that we will not be dissuaded from supporting Ukraine."

7) Colour detail: Kaliningrad described as "slightly bigger than the US state of Connecticut".
